newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan chipmakers expect 16MB DRAM prices to rise.
newsitem.headline: Japan chipmakers expect 16MB DRAM prices to rise.

text.p: Japan's major chipmakers said on Wednesday that they expect the market for 16-megabit dynamic random access memories (DRAMs) to improve due to a recent decision by South Korean chipmakers to cut output.

Despite the firmer outlook, Japanese chipmakers such as Toshiba Corp and Hitachi Ltd said they would maintain a cautious stance towards the market and would not raise their production of 16-megabit chips.

Three South Korean chipmakers, Samsung Electronics Co, LG Semicon Co and Hyundai Electronics Industries, said the decision to cut production later this month was partly in reaction to recent falls in international spot prices of chips.
Analysts said the move would tighten the oversupplied market and help raise market prices.

"Reduced output in July will tighten the supply/demand condition in the September-October period when demand increases ahead of the Christmas shopping season," said Hideki Wakabayashi, an analyst at Nomura Securities Co.

He said spot prices would likely rise above the current level of around $8 per unit as result of the output reduction, but that prices for large-lot users would likely remain at the current level of around $7-8 per unit.
Toshiba has gradually reduced its monthly output of 16-megabit chips to seven million units from February's peak of eight million, a spokesman said.
"At this point, we do not plan to alter our production of 16-megabit DRAMs because of the output reduction by South Korean makers," he said.
"South Korean makers' output cut will likely raise chip prices as it will tighten the market's supply-and-demand situation," he said.
A spokesman for Hitachi said the company also expects the production cut to have a positive impact but added that the company would not reverse its plan to reduce production.
The company plans to reduce monthly production of 16-megabit DRAMs to 10 million units by the end of this year from the current 11 million.

Meanwhile, Hitachi plans to boost production of next-generation 64-megabit chips from the current 300,000 units per month to three million units by April 1998 due to expectations that demand will increase.

NEC Corp also aims to raise production of 64-megabit DRAMs to four million units per month by the end of March 1998, while maintaining the monthly production of 16-megabit chips at 13 million units for the rest of this year.
